commit.message:
Blinks chat rooms on Blimp write the rows Phoenix writes, down to the IP hash

The same 18 steps in two tabs (two X-Forwarded-For addresses) against
Phoenix's /blinks and this /blinks-next, each on a fresh copy of
blog_blinks64_base, left the two databases with the same chatters
(screen_name, ip_hash, color shape), the same chat_messages (room,
sender, reply_to_id, md5 of content) and the same chat_message_votes.
14 steps show the same chat-window text in both tabs; the other 4 differ
only in the compose box after "click a name to @ them" (below).

The obvious identity is 65's: sha256(ip <> SECRET_KEY_BASE). That is
wrong here. Blog.Chat.hash_ip/1 is sha256(ip) with no secret, and every
chatters row was written with it; using 65's would make every returning
chatter a stranger. Both databases have alice's ip_hash d861b7e91033ebc1
for X-Forwarded-For 203.0.113.9.

Phoenix has no rate limit and no word filter on these rooms. The rules
are the changesets': name 1..20 and message 1..500 characters (graphemes,
Blimp #72), trimmed; a taken name gets 2, 3, ...; a reply to a reply
hangs off its top message, within the room. A 501-character message was
refused by both.

Over /live/blinks: a page that says {"t":"room"} joins the ROOMS topic
blink:<id> and is sent the last 100 messages with vote counts and its
own votes; sign_on/sign_off/say/vote are frames; new messages and counts
go to the room. Messages are rendered on the server as render_md/2 does
it (escape, demote #/##, strip javascript:/data:/vbscript:, new-tab
links, @mention spans); the page marks its own mentions "me".

One database, both servers: Blimp's tab was signed on as alice2, the
chatter Phoenix made for that IP, and showed Phoenix's history. A
message said on either server reached the other server's open tab only
after a reload: live delivery between two servers is not possible until
one of them serves both.

Differs on purpose: clicking a name to @mention it. In Phoenix that
changes the textarea's text but not its value once someone has typed in
it, so after typing (or sending) the box stays as it was:
  typed, then clicked a sender name:  phx "typed"   blimp "typed @alice2 "
  after send, clicked a sender name:  phx ""        blimp "@alice2 "
This fills the box every time.

Tests: test/blinks_chat_test.blimp (8), against a Rooms hub and a
stand-in for Postgres; ./build.sh test prints 42 lines, all "tests
passed".
